assumptions.text: 730 hours/month, region swedencentral, prices as of 2026-06-01
80% of steady-state on 1yr reserved instances
Azure Hybrid Benefit applied to Windows servers
one managed disk per VM sized to provisioned capacity; file shares, DB and object storage are priced separately (estimate_storage_cost)
all recommended SKUs priced
list rates as of 2026-09-01; USD/GB-month per category (source: injected rate book + estimation_config.json)
DB lines are the STORAGE component of a managed/PaaS database only — the database compute (vCores) and licensing are a replatform decision, sized separately
522 block volume(s) (161,376 GB) excluded — priced by estimate_compute_cost (one managed disk per VM). Set storage.price_block_from_storage_table to itemise them here instead.
233 powered-on servers counted (17 powered-off excluded)
backup: protected data x1.3 at $0.0224/GB-month + $5.0/instance
monitoring: 0.5 GB/server/day to Log Analytics at $2.3/GB + Defender for Servers
support plan: standard
one-time: dual-run 1.5 months at 50% of the $97,624/mo infra bill; migration tooling free for 180 days/server
excludes ExpressRoute / VPN, landing-zone fixed services, and DB compute (replatform) — those are separate proposal lines
CAF Azure Landing Zones architecture (platform + landing-zone management groups).
Environment spokes built per zone: prod, nonprod. DR region gets a mirrored address space.
A dedicated spoke + Confidential management group + CMK/private-endpoint policy overlay is created for each distinct regulated compliance scope in the portfolio.
Resiliency tier is derived from application criticality 1-4 -> 1/2/3/4 (RPO/RTO per estimation_config.json).
IP plan is a sequential carve of the configured supernet — reconcile against the client's real IPAM before build.
Appetite: rehost_first (replatform only criticality 3+ apps, <= 6 servers, no clustering).
6R candidate is rule-derived from the inventory — it is an input to the architecture board, not a decision. Repurchase / Refactor / Retire always need business sign-off.
Refactor is off (no refactoring this programme).
Platform / commodity dependencies (AD, DNS, NTP, monitoring — 362 edges) don't bind apps into a wave; the platform group migrates in the pilot wave and everything may depend on it.
Edges below 'low' confidence and flows not seen in 21 days are excluded (0 + 0 dropped) — confirm the move-groups against application SMEs.
Move-groups are connected components of the app dependency graph; groups are ordered low-risk-first, capped at 40 servers / 6 apps per wave, regulated scopes (HIPAA, HITRUST, PCI, PCI-DSS) last.
Non-production servers migrate ahead of production within each wave (5-day soak) — a scheduling note, not a separate wave.
Wave dates come from the duration model (E4.3), not this tool; blackout windows still apply.
All figures are DRAFT pending named-architect review; not a fixed price.

Landing-zone fixed platform services beyond the build effort
Database compute and licensing for replatformed PaaS databases
